name: Lennon Pereira
life: “I still remember being given a surname the waiting room couldn't safely hear.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Lennon watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I adopted a surname in adulthood. I want the clerk to ask which name a waiting room can safely call out.
appearance: Lennon has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Lennon counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Lennon finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To let patients choose the name called publicly.
family: Anton Wong is Lennon’s stepsibling. Lennon asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Anton chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Anton says, “I took in shirts as a child. I recognized the invisible mark our family always left inside a collar.”
connections: Marco Bennett. A safer printed band starts with asking which name the patient wants the room to hear.

reactions.situation: A clerk calls the wrong surname in the waiting room
reactions.response: Lennon waits for the patient to give a preferred public name before repeating it.
